answer: Each agent claims one anchor chain, posts a 70-credit bond, and files a key-bound link log. A raven inspector re-measures link wear, and an auditor recomputes the wear delta across measurements against a wear-rate table, burning the bond on mismatch or reuse. The first claim costs 33 credits; the kth costs 33+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6027 and 1000 fakes cost 3,030,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented-chain ring fails because a rented chain carries its owner's key and wear pattern, so its delta duplicates a filed log. An honest agent pays 33 once and keeps the bond refundable.
